content:
As macOS 27 Golden Gate is expected to officially launch later this year, Apple continues its beta testing efforts and has rolled out the fifth beta to developers. Here's a preview of what's in this update.

Apple releases macOS 27 beta 5

Three weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 4, followed by a corresponding public beta a few days later.

Now, Apple is pushing out macOS Golden Gate beta 5, continuing to fix bugs and improve performance ahead of this year's official release.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces an all-new Siri app, along with a redesigned Siri AI. The system also features a new AI-powered version of the Shortcuts app, allowing users to create shortcuts using natural language commands, and offers a prompt-based Safari extension builder.

In addition, macOS 27 Golden Gate adds new Golden Gate-style wallpapers and screensavers, while restoring the corner radius of windows and apps to a fixed size. This change reverses the approach taken in macOS 26, where the system previously adjusted the corner radius based on the content of each window or app's menu bar.

macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 carries the build number 26A5406e. We are currently diving into this new beta and will share our findings with you later.

How to install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" icon next to "Beta Updates"
  • Select "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta" from the dropdown menu in the top right
  • Click "Done"

Have you discovered anything new in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
